findings.desc: dangling-cross-ref: §2.2 referenced but does not exist — §1.2 (line 17) and §1.3 (line 23) both cite §2.2 for the independence-test definition, but Section 2 has no numbered subsection 2.2; the independence test is defined under the unnumbered Step 2 heading. Reader directed to a non-existent anchor.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: both §2.2 citations (lines 17, 23) changed to '§2, Step 2', the actual heading where the independence test is defined.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.4 — evaluateDecompositionGate(story, peers, contracts, cfg) has no TypeScript types for `peers` or `contracts` parameters; an implementer reading the spec cannot write a type-safe call from canStartDevGuard. `peers` must be StoryInfo[] filtered from store; `contracts` must be Map<string,ScopeContractData|null> or similar — neither is stated. This gap forces guesswork or `as any` at the call site.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: evaluateDecompositionGate signature now typed — story: StoryInfo, peers: StoryInfo[], contracts: Map<string, ScopeContractData>, cfg: ParallelGateConfig; added a note that canStartDevGuard must load peers+contracts before the (pure) call.

findings.desc: dangling-cross-ref: §4.5 reference misleading — line 65 in Step 2 (Section 2) says "see §4.5 / §7-F4" for the point that actualFileOverlapsByStory() cannot produce meaningful results pre-DEV, but §4.5 (The one new schema field) covers schema field placement for depends/dependsMeta and says nothing about pre-DEV probe semantics. The only relevant material on this topic is in §4.2 and the F4 row in Section 7.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: line 65 cross-ref changed from '§4.5 / §7-F4' to '§4.2 / §7-F4' (§4.2 holds the pre-DEV probe semantics).

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.4 line ~333 — self-contradictory catch-branch description for the new decomposition check inside canStartDevGuard. The text says the try/catch is "consistent with the guard's existing catch { return false } shape but inverted to fail-open". These two clauses contradict each other: the existing guard is fail-closed (return false); the new code must be fail-open (return true). An implementer following the first clause writes a fail-closed catch; following the second writes fail-open. Both cannot be true simultaneously. The correct intent (fail-open) must be stated unambiguously without the "consistent with" hedging, or the spec will produce incorrect implementations.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: reworded to state the new sub-check fails OPEN (returns true) — explicitly the opposite of the surrounding guard's fail-closed catch; removed the contradictory 'consistent with' hedging.

findings.desc: dangling-cross-ref: §4.4 says "fail-open, §4.7" but the fail-open/fail-closed policy is actually in §4.8 — line 333 in §4.4 writes "Wrap in try/catch returning true (fail-open, §4.7)" but §4.7 is the Config validation set section; the failure-mode guardrails including the fail-open rule are defined in §4.8. The §4.7 reference sends readers to the wrong section for the cited behavior.

quality-cleanup: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.2 / §4.3 — globsOverlap(a, b) return field `broad` is ambiguous. The function receives two write-sets; either or both could be broad. The spec says `broad: boolean` with no indication of whether it means (a is broad), (b is broad), or (a OR b is broad). Callers in evaluateDecompositionGate need to know which story has the broad glob to produce an actionable block message naming the colliding storyId. A single boolean loses this attribution. The parameter types for a and b are also not specified (presumably string[] from computeWriteSet but the spec omits them).

quality-cleanup: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.7 — parallelGate nested object in AuditConfig is not type-safe under the existing readUserConfig pattern. The current code does `return parsed as Partial<AuditConfig>` and then validates each scalar field individually (e.g., VALID_MODES.has(userOverrides.mode as AuditMode)). Adding a nested `parallelGate: { mode, maxConcurrentReview, broadGlobBlocks }` object is NOT handled by this pattern: an implementer following the existing scalar approach would likely write `merged.parallelGate = userOverrides.parallelGate ?? profileDefaults.parallelGate` — which bypasses all per-field validation and allows invalid mode strings through without the promised console.warn+fallback. The spec says validation is "copied from deprecatedGcThreshold" but those are top-level scalars; no code sketch is given for validating the nested struct. This is a doc-promise-undelivered gap: the spec promises per-field validation semantics for the nested object but gives no implementation path that achieves it.

doc-code-drift: spec §4.7 states VALID_MODES is typed to Set<AuditMode> but actual code in audit-config.ts declares it as ReadonlySet<AuditMode>. The logical conclusion (cannot be reused for parallelGate validation) is correct but the stated type annotation is factually wrong.

doc-code-drift: all scope_boundary_set examples throughout the spec (§3.1, §3.2, §3.3, §5.1–5.4, §6, §8) omit the required userConfirmed parameter. The CLI schema (cli-engine.ts) declares userConfirmed: z.boolean() without .optional(), and the handler throws 'userConfirmed must be true before the INIT scope boundary can be saved' when absent. Any agent copying these templates verbatim will get a validation failure (safeParse exit code 1).

doc-code-drift: all scope_contract_set examples in the spec (§3.1, §3.2, §3.3, §5.2, §5.3, §5.4, §6, §8) omit the required --mode parameter. The CLI schema (cli-engine.ts line 1976) declares mode: z.enum(['local','shadow','enforce']) without .optional() or .default(), so safeParse fails with 'Invalid enum value' when mode is absent. The handler defaults to 'enforce' (line 161 of scope-contract.ts), but that default is never reached because safeParse blocks first.

doc-code-drift: spec §4.4 item 4 says 'handlers/lattice-parallel-wave.ts — resolveWaveSafety gains a scope_glob_overlap degradation kind'. However resolveWaveSafety is a non-exported private function in core/lattice-parallel-wave.ts (line 751), not in handlers/lattice-parallel-wave.ts. The handler file imports from core but does not expose resolveWaveSafety. A developer following the spec would edit the wrong file.
